title: 8th Pay Commission: Understanding the 3.5x Fitment Factor Impact
description: The 8th Pay Commission is expected to revise salaries and pensions for central government employees and pensioners, typically once every decade. A key compone.

faq.q: Who does the Pay Commission cover?
faq.a: The Pay Commission's recommendations primarily cover central government employees, including those in the armed forces, All India Services, and Union Territories, as well as central government pensioners.

faq.q: What is the difference between basic pay and gross pay?
faq.a: Basic pay is the fixed component of your salary, forming the base for other calculations. Gross pay is your total salary before any deductions, comprising basic pay plus all allowances like DA, HRA, TA, etc.

faq.q: Will private sector salaries also increase?
faq.a: While Pay Commission recommendations directly apply only to government employees, a significant hike often creates a ripple effect, influencing salary expectations and revisions in the private sector to some extent, especially for comparable roles.

faq.q: How often are Pay Commissions constituted?
faq.a: Historically, Pay Commissions are constituted roughly once every ten years to review and revise the salary and pension structures for central government employees.

faq.q: What is the role of Dearness Allowance (DA)?
faq.a: Dearness Allowance (DA) is a cost-of-living adjustment paid to government employees and pensioners to offset the impact of inflation. It is revised periodically based on the Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers (CPI-IW) and is calculated as a percentage of basic pay.

faq.q: Will my taxes increase with a higher salary?
faq.a: Yes, a higher gross salary could potentially push you into a higher income tax bracket, leading to a larger tax liability. It's crucial to review your tax planning strategies under the Income Tax Act to optimise your tax outflow.
